column3: n. 独裁者
column5: The aging autocrat jailed journalists who questioned his decrees.
column6: 年迈的独裁者监禁质疑其法令的记者。

column3: vt. 装饰, 修饰
column5: Villagers bedeck the streets with lanterns before the harvest festival.
column6: 收获节前,村民们用灯笼装点街道。

column3: a. 逃避现实的;n. 逃避现实者

column6: 下班后,护士们靠逃离现实的小说解乏。

column3: a. 有义务的; 必须的; 有责任的;v. 使负有责任或义务（ obligate的过去式和过去分词 ）

column5: The gallery's eclecticism ranges from folk art to video installations.
column6: 这家画廊包罗万象,从民间艺术到影像装置。

column3: a. 一致的, 符合的, 同时发生的
column5: The rise in unemployment was coincident with the collapse of tourism.
column6: 失业率上升与旅游业崩溃恰好同时发生。

column3: n. 语文学, 文献学
column5: Classical philology requires patient study of handwritten medieval manuscripts.
column6: 古典语文学需要耐心研究中世纪手抄本。

column3: a. 火的, 似火的, 火成的
column5: Igneous rocks form when molten magma cools and solidifies.
column6: 火成岩由熔融岩浆冷却凝固而成。

column3: n. 旋回, 回转, 旋转;回旋, 环旋

column6: 滑冰者急速的旋转引来观众阵阵惊叹。

column5: Careful owners ensure their pets do not defecate on the running track.
column6: 细心的主人确保宠物不在跑道上排便。

column6: 加热血清可使大部分残留病毒灭活。

column3: n. 探矿, 勘探

column6: 淘金热曾把成千上万的家庭引向冰封的北方。

column3: vt. 使衰弱
column5: Repeated malaria attacks can debilitate a child for months.
column6: 疟疾反复发作能让孩子虚弱数月。

column6: 长期饥饿连最壮实的少年也会消瘦。

column3: v. 掩饰, 假装不知道
column5: Caught officials often dissemble rather than admit simple mistakes.
column6: 被抓住错处的官员往往遮遮掩掩,不认低级失误。

column3: n. 硅酸盐;硅酸盐; 硅酸酯
column5: The lunar soil is rich in silicate minerals similar to earth's.
column6: 月壤富含与地球相近的硅酸盐矿物。

column3: vt. 使狂喜
column5: The violin solo seemed to enrapture the entire concert hall.
column6: 小提琴独奏仿佛令整座音乐厅如痴如醉。

column3: a. 懒惰的, 无痛的;无痛的
column5: The indolent heir let the family business drift into bankruptcy.
column6: 懒散的继承人任由家族企业滑向破产。

column3: vt. 使习惯于;vi. 生效
column5: Desert guides are inured to temperatures that floor ordinary travelers.
column6: 沙漠向导早已习惯让普通旅行者瘫倒的高温。

column3: a. 不能渗透的, 不能通过的;不透性
column5: The clay liner makes the landfill impermeable to rainwater.
column6: 黏土衬层使垃圾场不渗雨水。

column3: n. 忠诚, 忠贞, 忠实
column5: The barons swore fealty to the young king at the coronation.
column6: 加冕礼上,贵族们向年轻的国王宣誓效忠。

column3: n. 契约, 契据, 凹痕;vt. 以契约束缚
column5: Poor migrants signed indenture contracts promising years of unpaid labor.
column6: 贫穷移民签订契约,允诺多年无偿劳作。

column3: a. 盐水似的, 海水似的, 咸的;含盐度

column6: 咸涩的海风带来裸露泥滩的气味。

column6: 他毫无心机的笑容连谨慎的客户也放松下来。

column3: a. 迅速的, 敏捷的
column5: The crew made expeditious repairs before the storm arrived.
column6: 队员们赶在风暴来临前迅速完成抢修。

column3: n. 贪婪
column5: The report laid the firm's collapse squarely at the feet of avarice.
column6: 报告把公司倒闭直接归咎于贪婪。

column3: n. 不适合, 不一致, 不信奉国教
column5: Her bold nonconformity in dress set her apart in the conservative office.
column6: 她大胆不羁的着装在保守的办公室里格外扎眼。

column3: v. 混合
column5: The rules forbid brokers to commingle client funds with their own.
column6: 规定禁止经纪商把客户资金与自有资金混同。

column6: 批评人士警告,这场纷争可能使政党裂成两半。

column3: a. 不高兴的, 不平的
column5: The grouchy neighbor complained about every ball that landed in his yard.
column6: 脾气坏的邻居抱怨每个掉进院子的球。
